links.note: Definition item: a Constitution is the document laying down basic principles and laws. 30789 is the concept that enumerates exactly what such a document has to settle (type of government, rules and principles, franchise, dispute settlement); 30787 is only Ambedkar's point about use in practice, which this recall item does not touch.

The helium-filled case is about the original handwritten manuscript as a physical artefact of the drafting, which is 30791's 'identifiable people, defined period' material; not 30787, which is about the document's worth in use rather than its preservation.
'Living document' = built expecting revision, which is 30798. Kept apart from 30800, which I reserve for items about the amending procedure itself (debate, state consent).

The model answer's whole point is that equality before the law is guaranteed on paper but incompletely realised in practice - Ambedkar's test of whether people act according to the Constitution. Not 30805, which is the rights-and-duties pairing rather than the gap between text and practice.

Universal adult franchise from the start: 'who should have the right to vote' is named in 30789's description as one of the questions the framers had to answer. 30788 (planning during the struggle) supplies the motive but not the subject.

Asks whether the ideals are achieved and what citizens can do; 30801 is the concept in which the core values guide government AND citizens are expected to practise them. 30787 is the narrower Ambedkar remark, used for the equality-in-practice item.
Crossword clue for Fundamental Rights ('basic rights given to every citizen, like freedom and equality') - the rights half of 30805's rights-and-duties pairing.

Tests that vasudhaiva kutumbakam is an Indian civilisational inheritance and NOT a modern Western import, which is exactly 30806. 30792/30793 are about borrowing from other constitutions, the opposite direction to what the false Reason claims.
Statement item on whether amendment requires parliamentary debate - the amending process being itself bound by rules, 30800, not the foresight concept 30798.

Recall of Nandalal Bose leading the illustration team: the named people who physically made the document, 30791. 30806 is the meaning of the illustrations, which a different item in this file carries.
Meaning of Fraternity in the Preamble; 30801 is the concept in which the core values are concentrated in the Preamble.
Directive Principles traced to Ireland - a named country in 30793's list of constitutions studied. 30792 is the Rig Vedic framing of borrowing, not the borrowings themselves.
'WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA' is 30802 verbatim - authority coming from below rather than from a ruler.
Liberty/Equality/Fraternity traced to France, one of the constitutions named in 30793.
Match a constitutional feature to the country it was studied from (independent judiciary - US): 30793.
Tests that borrowing was not confined to Britain, i.e. the multi-country study in 30793.
Meaning of Secular as a Preamble value - 30801.
Which value is NOT in the Preamble: requires the Preamble's list of core values, 30801.
Calligrapher Prem Behari Narain Raizada - a named person in the physical making of the document, 30791.
Purpose of the gurukula/Ramayana illustrations is to connect the Constitution with India's heritage - 30806's claim, as against 30791 which is about who drew them.
Parts and Schedules increasing since 1950 is the document actually growing through amendment (30800), not the framers' anticipation of change (30798), and not specifically Part IV-A (30799).
Match-the-following pairing features with the American/French etc. constitutions: 30793. Stem is truncated in the bank but the surviving options are unambiguous about what is matched.
Match-the-following over Preamble terms (Fraternity, liberty of thought/expression) - the Preamble values concept 30801.
One-word recall of 'Constitution' as the document laying down a nation's basic principles and laws; paired with 30789 for the same reason as the MCQ form of this item.
Helium-filled glass case - the manuscript as artefact, 30791.
The body formed in 1946 is the Constituent Assembly; 30790 is the Assembly concept. 30791 is the drafting work it did, which this bare recall of the body's name does not reach.
Article 14 Right to Equality as a protected right of citizens - the rights side of 30805.
Rigorous debate and state consent in amending: the amending process being itself governed, 30800.

Asks which influences shaped the Constitution (struggle ideals, heritage, other nations - not monarchy). 30792 is the 'noble thoughts from every side' framing of multiple sources; 30793 is reserved for items naming a specific country's constitution.
Role of the executive (implements laws, runs administration) is stated inside 30794's separation-of-powers description; 30795 is the central/state/local tiers, a different axis.

Rajendra Prasad on respect for others' viewpoints and capacity for compromise as what makes democratic institutions work - the same 'depends on how people use it' point as 30787. Not 30790, which is Sinha's charge to the Assembly at the outset.
Which listed influences are genuine (hereditary monarchy is not): the multiple-sources framing, 30792, consistent with the other 'which influence' item in this file.
'Equality of status and of opportunity' is a Preamble phrase - 30801.
Matches illustration themes (gurukula, Ramayana, Gita, Nataraja) to Parts; the illustrations are the chapter's evidence for the civilisational inheritance, 30806.

The 1976 amendment of the Preamble (SOCIALIST, SECULAR) is an instance of the document being changed through amendment, 30800. Not 30799, whose description is specifically Part IV-A Fundamental Duties, a different 1976 change.

Public feedback invited on proposed laws and amendments: the item sits in the chapter's account of how amendment is conducted, so 30800. Rejected 30802, which is about the original enactment by the people's representatives rather than ongoing consultation.
Meaning of Liberty in the Preamble - 30801.
Meaning of Equality in the Preamble - 30801.
Meaning of Fraternity in the Preamble - 30801.
What the illustrations signify: rooting the modern framework in India's civilisational heritage - 30806 in almost the same words.
Short-answer twin of the Rajendra Prasad MCQ; qualities needed for democratic institutions to work = the Constitution judged by how it is used, 30787.
Balance between Centre and States is 30795's second sentence (some functions reserved to the centre, others assigned to the states); 30794 is the three organs, not the tiers.
Necessity of a constitution for a large, diverse country via the Kabaddi analogy - 30789's description names exactly that predicament and the questions it forced.
'Why does a country need a constitution' - the questions a constitution exists to answer, 30789.
The rulebook analogy is the chapter's device for why the founding questions had to be settled in advance - 30789.
Example of civilisational heritage shaping the Constitution - 30806.
